notes: Generated parity supported labels are advertised scope, not proof of readers/effects.
No implementation test/model/build/database/provider/outbound operation ran for this documentation audit.
Export declarations are lexical; helpers/types/proofs are not feature coverage.
30 read/helper tools and117 preparation operations come from frozen routing catalog; future build re-derives from trusted runtime contracts.

runtime_tools.name: results.select
runtime_tools.description: Build a result card from selected rows already returned by compatible list reads in the current turn. Use it to project or combine displayed rows, not to run a new query, compute a new total, or combine incompatible result types.

runtime_tools.name: people.query
runtime_tools.description: Search, count, or group people and households, including cohorts defined by stage, tags, skills, recorded-history existence, attendance counts, contact availability, or ministry membership. Use relational filters here when the request needs only cohort membership, not the underlying history records.

runtime_tools.name: people.get_many
runtime_tools.description: Read known person or household records with profile, contact, household, tag, skill, or background-check fields. It does not search by name or return interview, assessment, attendance, or other history.

runtime_tools.name: people.history.query
runtime_tools.description: Read actual interviews, individual assessments, commitments, notes, activities, or person-linked follow-up history for a people cohort. Use it for record content, dates, or outcomes, not for an existence predicate already handled by people.query or for Plant Intelligence reports.

runtime_tools.name: attendance.query
runtime_tools.description: Read event-specific attendance, RSVP, response-card, and linked follow-up evidence across people and meetings. Use people.query instead when only attendance counts are needed to define a cohort.

runtime_tools.name: tasks.query
runtime_tools.description: Search, count, or group tasks and checklist rows by status, priority, assignment, dates, links, prerequisites, milestones, or parents. It also exposes the task-template catalog and current phase-template suggestions; use tasks.get_many only when full task or checklist detail is needed.

runtime_tools.name: tasks.get_many
runtime_tools.description: Read known tasks with full descriptions, dependency identities, assignees, and checklist contents. It is unnecessary for fields already returned by tasks.query.

runtime_tools.name: tasks.assignees.search
runtime_tools.description: Resolve a named eligible task assignee to an account identity or inspect eligible assignment options. It is not a general people directory and is unnecessary when a retained account ID or known person ID already suffices.

runtime_tools.name: meetings.query
runtime_tools.description: Search, count, or group existing meetings by date, type, status, team, title, location, preparation state, or evaluation presence. It is not needed merely to create a new meeting unless existing-meeting evidence or a conflict check was requested.

runtime_tools.name: meetings.get_many
runtime_tools.description: Read known meetings with agenda, preparation checklist, notes, evaluation, and other full details. It does not search for or choose a meeting.

runtime_tools.name: teams.query
runtime_tools.description: Query ministry teams, roles, assignments, people by assignment, rosters, vacancies, leaders, responsibilities, and completion state. Use it for staffing relationships; people stages alone do not establish ministry assignments.

runtime_tools.name: teams.get_many
runtime_tools.description: Read known teams or roles with full details, roster, responsibilities, skills, time commitment, background-check requirement, and required training. Use teams.query first when the team or role identity is unknown.

runtime_tools.name: training.query
runtime_tools.description: Query training programs, role-derived requirements, and recorded completions by person, team, role, program, completion state, or date. It does not provide certification or background-check expiry dates.

runtime_tools.name: communication.query
runtime_tools.description: Search, count, or group messages, recipient deliveries, templates, or distinct recipients, including failure and retry evidence. Use communication.get_many when full message or template content is required.

runtime_tools.name: communication.get_many
runtime_tools.description: Read full subject, body, placeholders, and resend-relevant content for known messages or templates. It does not search for IDs or return per-recipient delivery rows.

runtime_tools.name: documents.query
runtime_tools.description: Search document-generation templates or generated-document metadata, including formats, placeholders, history, and download links. It does not read document contents.

runtime_tools.name: documents.read
runtime_tools.description: Read bounded text with citations from known generated PDF, DOCX, or XLSX documents. It does not search arbitrary uploads, local files, or the filesystem.

runtime_tools.name: wiki.search
runtime_tools.description: Search or browse visible published wiki articles and return ranked passages, article identities, and citation slugs. Use wiki.read_many for full surrounding article content.

runtime_tools.name: wiki.read_many
runtime_tools.description: Read bounded content for known visible wiki citation slugs, including section and reading-progress evidence. It does not search for articles.

runtime_tools.name: launch.query
runtime_tools.description: Read launch status, milestones, milestone-linked tasks, and journal events, including recorded blocking relationships. It does not reconstruct past task or staffing state from current records.

runtime_tools.name: intelligence.query
runtime_tools.description: Read stored Plant Intelligence assessments, insights, attestations, transitions, check-ins, feedback, or operational signals. Use it for stored report claims and report-time evidence, not individual People assessments or a newly generated judgment.

runtime_tools.name: notifications.query
runtime_tools.description: Read, count, or group the current account's notification feed by unread state, category, source, or entity. Reading the feed does not mark notifications read.

runtime_tools.name: files.inspect
runtime_tools.description: Inspect an authorized conversation-attached People CSV and return import-preview rows, duplicates, and validation issues. It does not import records or inspect arbitrary URLs, documents, or filesystem paths.

runtime_tools.name: people.commitment-download
runtime_tools.description: Return a download link for the document attached to a known commitment. Use people.history.query first when the commitment identity is unknown.

runtime_tools.name: context.get
runtime_tools.description: Read the authoritative current phase together with the server reference time, church-local date, and timezone. Use it when those shared facts are themselves needed, not when a domain query already handles the requested date period.

runtime_tools.name: calendar.resolve
runtime_tools.description: Resolve a relative date, period, weekday, omitted-year date, or local meeting time against the church clock and timezone. Use it when another capability needs explicit calendar bounds or DST-aware time resolution, but omit it when the target query natively handles the requested period.

runtime_tools.name: locations.query
runtime_tools.description: Search or list saved active meeting locations and return their identities, addresses, and capacity. Use it for venue discovery, not general facility or lease research.

runtime_tools.name: locations.get
runtime_tools.description: Read one known saved meeting location with its address, capacity, and active state. It does not search by name.

runtime_tools.name: templates.for_meeting
runtime_tools.description: Read the full invitation subject, body, and placeholders for a known meeting type, honoring the plant's visible template fork or default. It is the direct template reader for meeting invitations and does not send or prepare a message.

runtime_tools.name: actions.status
runtime_tools.description: Read the saved status and recorded step counts of the current conversation's existing review. Use it when whether the review was only prepared or later applied is uncertain; it does not provide email-delivery evidence.

named_preservation_variants.acceptance: One reviewed new-meeting plan contains create-meeting → add-guests → send-invitations. Add-guests binds the actual persisted meeting ID from the create result; send waits for add-guests and targets that meeting. Review exact type/local date/time/timezone/duration/location/audience, exclusions/deduplication, subject/body and outward effects. Crash/reconnect or invitation failure recovers existing created meeting and guests; same-plan retries never create a second meeting or invite completed recipients again. Inviting an already existing meeting uses communication.send instead. Recipe reuse re-resolves current facts and requires a new exact approval.
named_preservation_variants.decision: Preserve concrete dependency-output semantics and one coherent review; a generic multi-step-plan fixture is insufficient.

named_preservation_variants.acceptance: Select only exact source recipients with proven provider_delivery_failed, failed email status, nonempty provider external ID and no delivery/open/click evidence. Refuse legacy/null provenance, uncertain acceptance, bounced/suppressed/deleted-person/changed-email or already claimed sources. Limit each exact reviewed cohort to 100. Revalidate source, permission and suppression at provider-attempt acquisition. Atomically claim each source to one child retry recipient; repeats recover that same child. Freeze first outbound bytes and timestamp; reuse the same effect+child provider key. Refuse attempts after the 23-hour safety window from first attempt; never mint a replacement key to escape provider idempotency expiry.
named_preservation_variants.decision: Preserve eligibility, exact source/child claim and safe retry behavior. A generic send-message gate is insufficient.

named_preservation_variants.acceptance: Prepare one exact review of 1–10 explicitly selected unread notifications; deduplicate input identifiers; prove actor ownership and current unread state. Execute only that reviewed subset with idempotent receipts. Other unread notifications remain unread. A one-notification operation and mark-all operation do not substitute for the selected-subset variant.
named_preservation_variants.decision: Preserve one, selected and all as distinct scopes with a shared typed domain handler.
